evals.prompt: We tested two ads: one has a new hook, the other has a new hook AND a new CTA. Ad B won. Was the hook or the CTA responsible?
evals.expected_output: Should point out this test is confounded — with two variables changed at once in Ad B, you cannot attribute the win to either the hook or the CTA specifically. Should recommend re-running a cleaner test that isolates one variable at a time.
assertions: Identifies the test as confounded (two variables changed)
Explains why the win can't be attributed to a specific variable

evals.prompt: Our thumbnail test has only 200 views on each variant after 2 hours and one is ahead by a few clicks. Can we call it?
evals.expected_output: Should caution against calling the test this early — the sample size is small and the lead could be noise. Should recommend a pre-set minimum sample size or time window before deciding, and treating a close early result as inconclusive rather than a real winner.
assertions: Advises against calling the test early
Flags the small sample size as a reliability concern
Recommends waiting for a pre-set threshold before deciding
